data.design: From the bible and authored layout: nearly black irregular rock chambers, a substantial connected loop and blind recesses, with faint outlines and scattered pale stone seams for orientation. The southern mouth supplies the recognizable way back. Keep the visual scarcity of bearings; do not fill the interior with luminous runes, an altar or a revealed owner of the skull.

description:
The ancient skull’s mouth opens into a nearly lightless cave. Irregular chambers connect through a large loop and blind alcoves; faint rock edges and scattered pale seams give enough bearings to find the southern exit through the teeth. A narrow fissure at the northern end disappears beyond the available light but does not lead to another playable area. Exploring it does not award a reward or unlock a required route.

Gastly, Duskull, Shuppet, Haunter and Misdreavus occur through native cave encounters at levels 20–28. They can interrupt ordinary movement inside, not only a visible grass patch. The return path remains available, but finding it in the darkness is part of the danger.

Old parallel scratches cross a wall beneath mineral crust. Elsewhere the child notices wet stone without audible dripping. The source preserves that contrast through an inspection line rather than a new explanation of the cave. The existing ambient music is quieter and lower-pitched again; the cave has no drifting fog or separate background-sound loop.

The skull’s species, origin and relation to other lore remain open. This is a cave reached through an ancient skull, not an established shrine, boss arena or account of the sea’s dead.
